data.name: Anahit
data.gender_notes: Anahit is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The ancient Persian goddess Anahit is the deity of fertility, health, and the source of life-giving waters. She is the patron goddess of the Temples of Anahit and Ardavan in Armenia. The name Anahit carries the meaning “Goddess of fertility and water” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Persian, Arabic. Parents who choose Anahit usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of fertility and water and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Anahit is a symbol of nurturing, creativity, and the abundance of life. She represents the power of the feminine spirit and the cyclical flow of nature.
data.etymology: Anahit belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of fertility and water.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anahit total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: Anahit is a significant figure in Iranian history and mythology. She was a major deity in the ancient religious pantheon of the Near East, particularly in Iran and Armenia. Her name and role as a goddess of fertility, health, and life-giving waters indicate her influence on agricultural productivity, health, and overall prosperity. Her temples were important centers of pilgrimage and religious devotion.
data.spiritual_significance: Anahit represents the nurturing and life-giving forces of nature. She embodies the deeply ingrained cultural belief in the spiritual interconnectedness of human well-being, cultural development, and the abundance of natural resources. Her role as a goddess of fertility also underscores the significance of family, community, and the importance of procreation and continuity within societies. Ultimately, the spiritual significance of Anahit stems from her role as a provider of life, health, and abundance, emphasizing the interconnected web of these elements and their importance in human existence.
